STEP 1 - Scene: A lunch-style plate with three distinct components: mashed/roasted orange squash (left), a chicken or tuna salad with celery and red onion (center), and shredded raw carrot (right). Photographed from above at a slight angle.

STEP 2 - Ruler: A square white plate, roughly 26 cm across the visible width. Area ≈ 3.14 × (13)² ≈ 530 cm² (treating it as a round-equivalent). Food on the side plate at the top right is excluded.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Roasted/mashed squash (pumpkin-type)
- Chicken (or tuna) salad with celery, red onion, bits of carrot
- Shredded raw carrot

STEP 4 - Area (percent of plate area):
- Squash: ~13% (≈70 cm²)
- Chicken/tuna salad: ~20% (≈105 cm²)
- Shredded carrot: ~17% (≈90 cm²)
Total covered ≈ 50% of plate, consistent with the visible spread.

STEP 5 - Volume (area × height):
- Squash: 70 cm² × 3 cm ≈ 210 ml (chunky pieces, moderate height)
- Salad: 105 cm² × 2 cm ≈ 210 ml (loose pile)
- Carrot: 90 cm² × 2.5 cm ≈ 225 ml (airy shreds)

STEP 6 - Grams (bulk density):
- Squash: 210 ml × 0.7 ≈ 150 g (cut/mashed vegetable, somewhat dense)
- Salad: 210 ml × 0.9 ≈ 190 g (dense meat-based salad)
- Carrot: 225 ml × 0.5 ≈ 110 g (shredded, airy)

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Squash, cooked: ~40 kcal/100 g → 150 g × 0.40 ≈ 60 kcal
- Chicken/tuna salad (mayo-light, celery, onion): ~150 kcal/100 g → 190 g × 1.50 ≈ 285 kcal
- Raw carrot: ~41 kcal/100 g → 110 g × 0.41 ≈ 45 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Total ≈ 450 g and ≈ 390 kcal. This is plausible for a moderate plated lunch with no visible added oil or dressing beyond what is in the salad. Values are estimates; the salad's mayonnaise content is the largest uncertainty.
